subject: civics
question_text: What are the difficulties people face in a non-democratic country?
answer_text: People face various difficulties such as lack of security of life, freedom of expression, and no right to elect their government.
final_answer: In non-democratic countries, people are often at the mercy of autocratic rulers.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding multiple aspects of non-democratic regimes.

subject: civics
question_text: Which freedoms are usually taken away when a democracy is overthrown by the military?
answer_text: Freedoms such as the right to freedom of speech, the right to form associations, and the right to have free elections are usually taken away.
final_answer: These freedoms are essential for a functioning democracy.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the implications of military rule on civil liberties.

difficulty_reasoning: Requires critical thinking about global democracy and power dynamics.

subject: civics
question_text: Discuss the implications of wealth and size of nations on their influence in international affairs and democracy.
answer_text: Wealthy nations will have a greater say in international affairs. They cannot let their interests suffer just because they are outnumbered by poor nations. Big countries like India must have a greater say in international organisations. If any country gives more money to international institutions and its citizens want more respect and more power, it would not contribute to democracy at the global level. Every country and its citizens enjoy equal status whether it is a poor or a rich country. Equality is the basic principle of democracy. If any country is small or poor but its citizens are treated equally and their voice is heard with equal respect it will promote equality and freedom of expression. If this is done at the global level, then this will definitely contribute to democracy at the global level. Because of these two facts we can say that the position of equality is nearer to democracy. The third position would also not lead to democracy at the global level because there should be no distinction between the rich nations and the poor nations. Otherwise, it will not help in bringing socio-economic equality which is one of the important aspects of democracy. At the global level, all the countries, whether poor or rich, should be treated at par with each other. The last position would also not contribute to democracy at the global level because the sizes or the geographical area of a country should not be a condition of superiority. However, in my opinion, in international organizations like the UN, the General Assembly should become like a world parliament with representatives from each country in proportion to the population of the country.
final_answer: In conclusion, equality among nations, regardless of wealth or size, is essential for promoting democracy at the global level.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of global democracy principles and socio-economic factors.
